title: Understanding Self
text:
The Baseline
Finding yourself isolated on an island with only the open ocean ahead forces an audit of how you arrived. Historically, my default posture was to dive straight in and improvise the mechanics on the fly. That worked when the arena had established boundaries—when the career path still provided invisible training wheels.
Frontier AI shifts that equation. Used deliberately, modern computational intelligence acts as an equalizer and a cognitive lever, expanding the operational horizon far beyond formal specialization.
That realization triggered a distinct memory: standing at a crossroads after completing undergraduate studies in aerospace engineering. The safe path was to remain anchored in my full-time job. The open ocean was pursuing a doctorate in medicinal chemistry. Rather than choosing containment or expansion, I chose both—working full-time while completing the PhD.
Decades later, that same fork has reappeared. The difference this time is sovereignty: I am no longer navigating someone else’s institution or defined research tracks. The goal is charting what I actually want to build, and heading straight into open water.

title: Preparing for the Journey
text:
Preparing to Navigate Blue Ocean
A blue ocean represents uncontested territory—an expansive operating space with little to no competition for resources. On the island, security is familiar, but the perimeter is finite and extractive. Looking out past the reef means choosing infinite potential over managed constraint, recognizing that self-determination in uncharted waters requires an entirely different operational posture.

title: Preparing for the Journey
text:
Gathering Provisions
Navigating genuine uncertainty cannot be solved by simply accumulating static provisions. Stockpiling supplies works only when you know the destination and duration of the voyage; confronting an emergent horizon demands dynamic capability over passive inventory.
Instead of hoarding consumables, provisioning here means engineering adaptive instruments:

Sensory Telemetry: Building reliable feedback loops across somatic signals, biometric baselines, and data streams.
Cognitive Architecture: Structuring mental models and local computational workflows capable of stress-testing assumptions.
Navigational Resilience: Developing the capacity to identify, extract, and synthesize new resources as conditions evolve, mapping viable paths forward in real time.

title: N-1 Experiments
text:
N-1 Experiments
Case Study



The Opportunity
I envision myself on a deserted island, looking out across the vastness of the blue ocean. The island represents current, bounded opportunities. One can live well enough, but the perimeter imposes subtle limits on every dimension of life.
The blue ocean represents unconstrained potential: the island is what is known or nearly exhausted, while the open water represents uncharted territory.






NoteThe Navigational Imperative



The modern landscape runs on extraction: attention, cognitive autonomy, vital energy, and capital. I am stepping outside those captured currents—moving ahead of the crowd to chart an intentional passage across open water. Instead of curating a retrospective after the journey is done, I am publishing the raw telemetry, navigational logs, and tools in real time.


The Problem

Trying to navigate the blue ocean forced a re-examination of my life, formal training, and career to this point. In truth, confronting this scale of opportunity revealed I was still riding with training wheels.
The Current Approach

The vastness of the open water beckons, thrills, and intimidates in equal measure. The past two to three years have served as an intentional liminal phase—an extended period of preparation.
This is why I use N=1 Experimentation to describe this operational methodology. Rather than adopting an inherited blueprint, the process begins by re-evaluating baseline identity and isolating the underlying why.
Understanding the ground underfoot is the first requirement before venturing outward. Whether the crossing proves worthwhile is judged by the navigator alone, and the voyage will inevitably take longer than planned.
Take what works for you as this work unfolds. The beauty of a blue ocean is that every heading is viable. Even modest coastal voyages undertaken while maintaining a conventional career are entirely valid—including simply casting a line from the shore.
Areas of Interest



Self
Understanding Self
On this path and going forward, you set the direction and length of the journey.



Preparation
Getting Ready for the Journey
Resources, tools, models, and provision architecture.



Navigating the Waters
Sailing the Open Sea
Navigation signals, ocean swells, and weather. Using pattern recognition to read the signals, predict shifts, and navigate emerging conditions.



Map the Journey
Mapping the Paths
Recording your journey, sights, feelings, and findings. Building return routes and paving the way for other like-minded travelers.


The Approach
The methodology I developed integrates multiple domains:

Multiple data sources — Don’t trust any single framework. Draw from many: analytics and intuition, conventional and unconventional, conscious and somatic.
Pattern recognition — Look for convergence and resonance. When several independent signals point in the same direction, that overlap is meaning. Not proof—but signal worth investigating.
Biomarkers — Your body knows before your mind does. Energy levels, time perception, emotions, physical sensations—all are data. That drained feeling despite success? That’s not a character flaw. That’s a system alert.
Quantified self — Track your experiences. You cannot find a pattern in a dataset that doesn’t exist.
AI and operational tooling — Read the weather, test assumptions against models, and chart clear passage toward your objectives.

title: David Howe
text:
I’ve spent most of my career modeling biological systems in pharma—teaching myself to see the hidden patterns that predict how drugs behave in the human body.
My job was finding patterns and projecting the story: what dosage works, where it’s safe, how often to give the drug. I was good at it. Companies still bring me on to consult and model their potential drugs.
And every time I do it, I feel the same thing: competent… and drained.
That observation—being successful by every external measure while feeling hollow inside—became the first data point in a different kind of modeling project. One where I am the system being studied.

The same methodology I used to decode molecular behavior could decode the behavior of my own meaning:

Multiple data sources — Don’t trust any single framework
Pattern recognition — Look for convergence across independent signals

This is “here’s how I am finding mine—use the approach to find yours.”

title: David Howe
text:
What I’m Building
Fire in the Cave is the methodology applied at multiple scales:
Personal — How to detect your own patterns, navigate your own alignment, find what actually energizes rather than drains you.
Systemic — The same pattern recognition that reveals personal standing waves also reveals collective ones. Education, finance, geopolitics—anywhere manufactured motion masquerades as progress.
Architectural — Eventually, the tools themselves.
Same fire. Different scales.

This site is built with Quarto and hosted on GitHub Pages—tools I control, that I could move if needed. Practicing what I’m preaching.

title: Collaborations & Advisory
text:
Collaborations & Advisory
Data Systems, Cognitive Infrastructure & Model-Driven Sensemaking


The Operational Posture
Most artificial intelligence initiatives fail because they treat models as conversational novelties or drop-in replacements for human critical thought. They automate superficial tasks while outsourcing cognitive autonomy to centralized cloud monopolies.
My advisory work approaches data and computational intelligence through an engineering lens:

Treating AI as a high-leverage cognitive lever that expands what an individual or lean team can model, test, and execute.
Building data sovereignty—anchoring private intelligence pipelines on local workstations and private clusters rather than leaking proprietary logic.
Translating disparate, noisy data streams into coherent navigational models for high-stakes decision spaces.

I partner selectively with founders, technical practitioners, and independent thinkers building at the frontier of complex systems.
Engagement Archetypes


01 / Architecture
Local AI & Infrastructure Sovereignty
Designing resilient, self-hosted LLM and agentic automation pipelines. Structuring multi-machine workflows (local orchestrators, private vector vaults, n8n automation) to ensure complete data provenance and zero cloud capture.


02 / Synthesis
Multi-Domain Data & Pattern Synthesis
Extracting signal from noisy environments. Integrating disparate telemetry—market dynamics, system metrics, and operational logs—into unified decision models and custom dashboards.


03 / Strategy
High-Context Advisory & Decision Stress-Testing
Structured sparring sessions to interrogate architecture, pressure-test assumptions, and evaluate the second- and third-order impacts of technological acceleration on your organization.


Operational Principles
Engagements are structured around rigorous execution rather than endless retainer meetings:

Sovereign by Design — Proprietary strategy and workflows stay on your machines. We prioritize local weights, private networking, and deterministic execution over black-box vendor lock-in.
Asynchronous Depth — Deep work happens through structured artifacts, Quarto technical briefs, and clear system specifications, minimizing conversational fatigue.
Signal Over Hype — We cut through vendor narratives to evaluate what frontier models and analytical methods can mathematically and pragmatically accomplish today.

Initiating an Engagement or Dialogue
I evaluate inquiries strictly on signal density, clear framing, and alignment with the lab’s active operational models.








NoteAdvisory & Technical Engagements



For private advisory, infrastructure reviews, or system stress-testing, outline:

The Core Bottleneck: The specific analytical, automation, or data sovereignty friction.
Current Substrate: Your hardware, data formats, and active tooling.
Target Horizon: The exact capability or sovereign pipeline you need to deploy.












NoteMedia & Long-Form Discourse



For technical podcast appearances, panel dialogues, or long-form interviews:

Platform & Audience: The forum and technical depth of the listenership.
Core Inquiry: The specific thesis, cross-domain pattern, or paper to dissect.
Format & Timeline: Recording timeline and technical constraints.

title: Sailing the Open Sea
text:
Navigating Beyond the Horizon
Once you clear the reef, the safety rails of defined roles and inherited structures disappear. Sailing the open sea means operating in genuine uncertainty—where progress is measured not by adhering to a fixed schedule, but by reading shifts in conditions and responding with deliberate maneuver.

title: Sailing the Open Sea
text:
Reading Swells & Weather
Navigating complex systems requires treating environmental turbulence as signal rather than friction:

Pattern Recognition — Reading cross-currents and macro trends before they solidify into consensus.
Matched Filtering — Distinguishing systemic noise from actionable signal through calibrated baseline telemetry.
Sovereign Maneuver — Maintaining operational flexibility to tack when conditions dictate, rather than stubbornly fighting the swell.
